text.en: A short poem tells of children who each have a few crayons. One needs red, the other needs black. When they share, they have a full pack. In this chapter you will think about sharing, say words that begin with sounds like gr and cr, learn action words, put words in alphabetical order and make new words by joining two words.

The poem is about children who each have some crayons, but not all the colours. One child needs the red crayon and the other needs the black crayon. If they share, together they have a full pack of crayons. The poem teaches that sharing helps everyone, because together we have more than alone.
Some words begin with two letters that we say together, such as gr, cr, dr and pr. Gr words include green, grey, grass, grapes and grandmother. Cr words include crayon, crab, crane, crow and cradle. Dr words include draw, drum, dress, drop and dragon. Pr words include prince, princess, prize, pray and present. Say each word slowly and listen to how it starts.
Words that tell what someone does are called action words. Examples are laugh, dance, eat, cry, swim, sleep, play, dig, jump, run, write, smile and push. Words like carrot, leg, book and cat are not action words, because they name things. To find an action word, ask: can someone do it? You can jump and you can write, so these are action words.
There are 26 letters in the English alphabet, from A to Z. Putting words in alphabetical order means arranging them by their first letters, in the order of the alphabet. Apple, banana, cherry, grapes and orange are in alphabetical order because A comes before B, B before C, C before G and G before O. If two words begin with the same letter, we look at the second letter.
Two small words can join to make one new word. Such a word is called a compound word. Rain and bow make rainbow. News and paper make newspaper. Basket and ball make basketball. Earth and worm make earthworm. Blue and berry make blueberry.

problem.en: Put these in alphabetical order: yellow, blue, purple, green, red.

text.en: Look at the first letters: Y, B, P, G, R.
In the alphabet the order is B, G, P, R, Y.

why.en: Blue comes first, then green, purple, red, yellow.

text.en: So the order is blue, green, purple, red, yellow.

problem.en: Which of these are action words: laugh, book, swim, leg?

text.en: Ask whether someone can do it.

why.en: A person can laugh and swim.

text.en: Book and leg name things.
The action words are laugh and swim.

prompt.en: Explain what an action word is and give three examples.

requiredIdeas.en: Action words tell what someone does

commonMisconceptions.en: A noun is an action word
